claims.statement: Order book as of 31 March 2024 stands at Rs 22,652.68 crore, mainly shipbuilding orders including P17 Alpha, Survey Vessel Large, ASW Shallow Water Craft, and NGOPV projects.
Management confident of sustaining PAT margins around 7.5% and current higher margin levels in coming years.
Revenue growth target of over 20-25% year-on-year for the next two years (FY25 and FY26).
Internal shipbuilding capacity being expanded from 20 to 24 concurrent warships by end of calendar year 2024.

Declared L1 for Oceanographic Research Vessel (~Rs 840 crore), 1000 cu.m dredger for Bangladesh (~Rs 135 crore), Ocean-Going Tug for Bangladesh (~Rs 160-170 crore), and DRDO Research Vessel (~Rs 500+ crore); contracts expected soon.

Expect RFPs for Next Generation Corvette (~Rs 36,000 crore, 8 ships), Coastal Research Vessels (~Rs 500 crore), 2 Multi-Purpose Vessels (~Rs 1,200 crore), and 5 Next Generation Survey Vessels (~Rs 3,000 crore) in near future.
Need fresh orders of Rs 20,000-25,000 crore by FY26 to sustain revenue tempo beyond 2027.
Current capacity allows concurrent construction of 20 warships (8 large, 12 medium/small); expanding to 24 by end of CY24; also using partner yards for part construction.

Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin ~8.9% (excl. other income), highest in several quarters; driven by lower subcontracting charges, better collection efficiency, revenue expenditure reduction, and overall efficiency improvement.
Management confident of sustaining current PAT margin levels (approx 10% in FY24) going forward, not just the 7.5% historical benchmark.
P17 Bravo Frigate RFP expected earliest by 2026; GRSE built 3 of 7 P17 Alpha ships; continuity in production anticipated.
Total order book stands at Rs 25,231.29 crore as on 30 June 2024, comprising 18 warships for Indian Navy, one Oceanographic Research Vessel, and four export projects.
P17 Alpha project order value enhanced to Rs 21,000 crore from initial Rs 19,293 crore; Rs 14,392 crore remaining to be executed.
Targeting 25-30% revenue growth in FY25 and similar growth in FY26; FY26 likely to be peak revenue year.
Aim to maintain PAT margins of 7.5-8% on yearly basis despite revenue growth; quarterly fluctuations possible due to project maturity.
Shipbuilding capacity to increase from 20 to 24 concurrent platforms by end of calendar year 2024; three dry docks leased from Kolkata Port Trust for ship repairs.

Capacity enhancement initiated: one shipbuilding unit completely revamped to raise concurrent capacity to 24 by end CY2024; three dry docks leased from Kolkata Port Trust; PPP model with private yards for concurrent construction.
Order book stands at ₹24,221.37 crore as of 30 September 2024, comprising 12 projects with 43 platforms including 4 export projects with 10 platforms.

P17 Alpha balance order ₹13,927 crore; ASW SWC ₹4,331 crore; Survey Vessel Large ₹729 crore; NGOPV ₹3,023 crore; Oceanographic Research Vessel ₹796 crore; Multipurpose Vessels ₹520 crore; Bangladesh export projects ₹314 crore; Naval Surface
Revenue CAGR of around 25% targeted for FY23-FY27 period; confident of maintaining or exceeding this growth rate.
Shipbuilding margins optimal at 7.5-8% in competitive environment; confident of maintaining similar margins; ship repair margins better and could lift blended margins as revenue share rises.
Gross margin decline in Q2 due to project maturity phase where material cost rises from 65-70% of value at 40-60% physical progress; natural phenomenon in shipbuilding cycle.
Target to achieve concurrent construction capacity of 28 ships by 2025; currently at 24.
